_readme: User-visible changes in the replacement app, newest first.

entries.summary: Memory tip sheet text gets side padding
detail: Text no longer touches the sheet's left edge.

entries.summary: Fix: Memory tip sheet now shows its explanation (the body had collapsed to nothing)
detail: The sheet's text area had no height, so only the title showed. It now sizes to its content.

entries.summary: Fix: Memory tip tile now actually appears (it was reading the wrong language variable)
detail: The first release looked up the language by a name that does not exist, so no card ever got a tip. It now uses selectedLanguage.

entries.summary: Memory tip tile on the card back shows how a word's ending maps to English (rápidamente → rapidly)
detail: New Memory tip tile beside Rarer uses; opens a small sheet naming the shift, e.g. -mente becomes -ly, -ción becomes -tion.
Spanish, Portuguese and French endings; a tip appears only when the card's own English gloss really wears the English ending, so false friends such as actualmente and chica get none.
Shown on any matching card, not only with Smart Skip off.

entries.summary: Noun forms merge only when every dictionary sense matches and both words have one noun entry
detail: Keep ser/seres and poder/poderes separate: noun and verb entries remain distinct even when their headword spelling matches.
Compare complete original SpanishDict and Wiktionary menus before filtering or display inflection; reject missing evidence and number-specific senses.
Invalidate earlier noun approvals and preserve the same decision in Smart Skip, deck grouping and early-loading indexes. Existing releases need refreshed source metadata to approve noun pairs.

entries.summary: Polish landing layout: prominent titles, level scrubber badge, target example words, card range nomenclature, centered modals
detail: Header titles are enlarged and capitalized (Choose a Level, Choose a Set, Practice Errors).
Level picker features an illuminated focal badge on the active level, removes redundant header level label, and places speech coverage inline after target-language example words.
Retired 'Set 1, 2, ...' in favor of card ranges (e.g. 1–25) across selectors, buttons, loading screens, and completion modals.
Refactored setup tooltip modals to be concise, scannable, and cleanly centered across both mobile and desktop viewports.

entries.summary: Inflected Portuguese rows drop dictionary notes and inflect every meaning: está 'he/she is', not 'he/she is; forms the progressive aspect'
detail: Notes beside the meanings are left off inflected rows: 'forms the progressive aspect', 'formula used in greetings', 'especially…', 'usually', 'such as…'. vai: 'he/she is doing; formula used in greetings' → 'he/she is doing'.

Meanings written without 'to' now inflect too: busca 'he/she fetches, pick up' → 'he/she fetches, picks up'; tira 'takes, take out, take away' → 'takes, takes out, takes away'; cola 'sticks or attach' → 'sticks or attaches'.
Alternatives after 'to be' stay as they are ('he/she is absent, not present'); an object alternate stays ('starts an engine, vehicle').
Measured on live v23: 232 Portuguese rows changed, no Spanish row changed, none lost its English.

entries.summary: Early level estimates suggest a particular study set
detail: Suggest a level and set within Levels 1–10, using the same 25-position set boundaries as the study picker; from Level 11 suggest whole levels.
Keep earlier and later options separate when they land in different sets of the same level, and select the chosen set after its controls finish loading.
Sample more finely near the start of the frequency range while keeping the adaptive check at up to 30 questions and preserving saved Speech-rank placement.

entries.summary: INFLECT pass 2: reflexive rows and feminine/plural participles get inflected English; conjugation table finds -se forms
detail: Spanish -se rows inflect: siento (sentirse) 'to feel' → 'I feel'; fue (irse) 'to leave' → 'he/she left'; acuerdo (acordarse) → 'I remember'. 2,000 rows on 1,183 card/verb pairs.

Feminine and plural participles inflect: pt feita → 'made', querida → 'loved', mortos → 'killed'; es muertos → 'died'. 341 pt rows, 77 es rows. Only when the word is not also an ordinary verb form (pt pega stays 'he/she catches').

Conjugation table on a -se verb opens on the card's tense and highlights its form: fue with irse selected now opens Pretérito on 'se fue' (was: present tense, nothing highlighted). The pronoun stays in the table: 'me siento'.
Measured on live v23 decks: no existing row changed and none lost its English; only rows that showed the infinitive gained one.
Known: 3 pt rows read 'been' (feita under fazer's weather sense) — a sentence-assignment issue upstream, not inflection.

entries.summary: Choose an earlier or later estimated starting point
detail: Offer a more conservative starting level near 90% recognition and a later level near 80%, showing how familiar the vocabulary is likely to be.
Use the same cognate decisions as Smart Skip for estimation even when Smart Skip is off; qualifying cognates never appear as questions.
Show AUTO under levels covered by the saved estimate, without recording estimator answers as learned cards or changing actual study progress.

entries.summary: INFLECT pass 1: conjugated verb rows read as natural English (era → 'I was', parece → 'he/she seems')
detail: Imperfect and past subjunctive are simple past, never progressive: era 'I/he/she was being' → 'I/he/she was', tenía 'was having' → 'had'.
A form that is both a statement and a command shows the statement: parece 'seem! / he/she seems' → 'he/she seems'. The command shows only when the example is one ('Let's go!' → let's go!).
When the example says I or he/she, the row uses that person: era + 'I was a very different person then.' → 'I was'.
English spelling fixed: meaned → meant, runing → running, planed → planned, lended → lent, hurted → hurt (full irregular table + consonant doubling).
Wiktionary glosses keep every clause and whole brackets: vi 'I saw (to be able to see' → 'I saw (to be able to see; not to be blind or blinded)'; faço 'I play' → 'I play; pretend to be'.
Measured on live v23 decks: command clutter 2,264 → 0 (es) and 2,169 → 0 (pt); progressive imperfects 760/705 → 0; misspellings and broken brackets → 0.
Not yet: -se verbs (siento under sentirse), agreeing participles (feita), clitic forms (dime) still show the infinitive — counted for pass 2.

entries.summary: Song lyrics view: removed synthetic word-by-word line translations in favor of strictly authentic hand-translated lyrics
detail: Removed synthetic dictionary word concatenation from lyric lines: only verified hand-translated English subtitles are rendered underneath.
When no authentic human translation exists for a line, lyrics render in pure Spanish without artificial glosses.
Synced audio timestamps render directly alongside the original lyric text; topbar 'EN line' toggle button hides automatically when a song has no hand-translated lines.
Word, idiom, and entity quick-view modals retain full access to Fluency's hand-curated definitions and WSD sense assignments.

entries.summary: Level estimation follows merged forms and separate reading cards
detail: Estimate vocabulary groups using the same merge and selective split rules as Smart Skip, with pooled Speech frequency and the most common eligible prompt.
Split readings show a matching sentence and divide surface frequency; sibling answers remain independent.
Keep saved Speech-rank placement compatible, show preparation progress, and withhold legacy CEFR labels pending calibration.

entries.summary: Song lyrics view: clean underline-free elision styling and contextual TURBO-2 WSD sense disambiguation in lyrics inspector
detail: Removed dashed underlines on elided words in favor of clean text with soft-cyan styling, keeping lyric flow natural without hyperlink-like baselines.

Wired newly deployed TURBO-2 unified WSD decision logic into the lyrics quick-view modal so contextual senses (obligation, progressive, future, perfect, reflexive) are prioritized for each lyric line.
Added dictionary fallback in postProcess to match tokens against the engine dictionary even when filtered out of high-frequency playlist card cuts.

entries.summary: TURBO-2: Web Worker WSD pipeline and live Spotify playlist study deck generation
detail: Integrated unified UNISON WSD decision logic directly into client turbo-engine: progressive auxiliary, modal obligation, future auxiliary, perfect auxiliary, and reflexive clitic routing.
Created dedicated background Web Worker (app/js/turbo-worker.js) for non-blocking intake, normalization, and semantic sense assignment.
Updated live playlist import to stream background progress and assign playable Spotify clip timestamps to matched card senses.

entries.summary: Clearer return-to-study prompt, readable settings, and easier main-menu access.
detail: Centre the return prompt on phones and desktops, show the username and last card, and simplify the saved-set summary.
Keep last-card restoration and let the loading spinner paint before rebuilding the saved deck.
Use larger settings text and high-contrast neutral selections in dark and light themes.
Replace study gear icons with three dots and put Main menu and Study settings first.

entries.summary: Progress gets its own top-bar icon and a rebuilt overview
detail: Open progress directly from the top bar; language settings now focus on language and vocabulary.
A centred coverage ring, Known / Practice / New breakdown and expandable answer history replace the old statistics grid.
Immediate opening, retry, keyboard closing, phone scrolling and stale-response protection make the overview reliable.
Removed the misleading complete-sentence percentage based on a partially loaded example corpus.
Counts and coverage use deduplicated recorded knowledge, including reviews of individual meanings.

entries.summary: Song lyrics view: dual song selector with offline probe songs and live online TURBO intake (Spotify URL, track ID, search query, or manual paste)
detail: Added segmented picker tabs: choose between curated offline playlist (30 songs) or generate custom songs online with TURBO.
Online intake supports Spotify track URLs, Spotify track IDs (22 chars), song title & artist searches via LRCLIB, and direct manual lyrics paste.
Integrated client TURBO engine execution on the fly with live status progress, caching newly generated songs for seamless switching.
Added topbar shortcut pill '⚡ Online TURBO' and auto-detection of Spotify URLs in search inputs.

entries.summary: Study sets: larger rank numbers, brighter legend and darker skipped progress
detail: Removed the hash from each frequency range and enlarged the numbers with heavier weight and vertical padding.
Legend counts use the main text colour for clearer contrast.
Skipped cards use a darker slate-grey fill in set progress bars and the matching legend swatch.

entries.summary: Song lyrics view: Spotify-style minimalist layout with target lyrics, English subtitles underneath, mobile bottom-sheet, and Fluency design integration
detail: Replaced dense audit layout with Spotify-style minimalist lyrics flow: prominent target text in Space Grotesk with clean English gloss directly underneath.
Unified design system with Fluency's industrial dark palette (--bg-primary, --bg-card, --border-color, --font-emphasis).
Added mobile-first responsive bottom-sheet modal with drag handle and safe-area padding for one-handed inspection on phones.
Added topbar subtitle toggle pill ('EN line') to switch English line translation visibility.

entries.summary: Level Estimator audit: starting level placement fix, SENSE_CYCLE POS resolution, keyboard controls, and CEFR indicators
detail: Fixed off-by-one level placement where learners were routed to a 100% completed level; now routes to first unseen card.
Resolved SENSE_CYCLE part-of-speech handling so grouped nouns and verbs are sampled and labelled properly.
Increased shard candidate attempts to 48 to prevent premature aborts on columnar releases.
Added full keyboard shortcuts (Space/Enter to flip, 1/2 or Arrow keys to answer, Escape to close) and modal backdrop dismissal.
Added visual progress track and CEFR stage mapping on results screen.

entries.summary: Song lyrics view: interactive lyric reader with token quick-view, sense assignments, entities, and ad-libs
detail: Added lyrics-view mode accessible from learning settings and the artist setup card in lyrics mode.
Browse the 30-song offline playlist with searchable picker and song-by-song navigation.
Interactive lyric lines with automatic classification and inline badges for entities, idioms/MWEs, interjections/ad-libs, and vocabulary.
Quick-view modal inspecting surface elisions, primary sense assignments, entity cultural descriptions, and alternate Spanish senses with keyboard navigation.

entries.summary: Landing page: centred section labels and wider set cards in a 2 × 2 grid
detail: Choose level, Choose a set and Practice errors have equal spacing above and below their labels.
Set cards are about 20% shorter and arranged in two columns, with frequency rank ranges visible on phones and desktop.
The selected set retains its accent ring without enlarging or shifting the card.

entries.summary: Cards are no longer named after a phrase they appear in: é cites ser, not "não é"
detail: A card's dictionary form skips headwords with more words than the card's own word (não é on é, por qué on por, cinto de segurança on cinto), unless it is the same spelling written apart (porfavor).
Look up links on é now open WordReference and Reverso for ser; they searched "não é".
With Merge Lemmas on, the back of é reads ser, not "não é · ser"; não, por and do read não, por and de.
Same rule as the release's lemma column (11276edc), already live on es and pt v23.

entries.summary: UNISON post-audit release: metadata contract, clean possessives, split card partitioning, and MWE production cues
detail: Split cards: prevent Card 2 from repeating the whole Card 1 menu when it has no distinct primary senses; retain expression senses on base cards.
Card metadata pills: suppress grammatical jargon tags (transitive, intransitive, copular) while keeping companion prepositions, register, and regional badges intact.
English to target production: display [phrase] scope badge on multi-word expression prompts so learners know a phrase is expected.
Portuguese & Spanish decks: updated with Decision 0030 sense/metadata contract, cleaner possessives (seu -> your/his/her), and companion disambiguation (falar + com / + de).

entries.summary: Vocabulary choice: switching and progress carry-over stated; hover text says words start most common first
detail: Intro under 'Choose your flashcard vocabulary source' now ends: You can switch at any time, and the words you learn carry over between the two modes.
Desktop hover text on Everyday speech: 'Starts with the most common words in films and TV shows'; on Your music: 'Starts with the most common words in the music you listen to'.
The in-study vocabulary picker shares the intro wording.

entries.summary: One tutorial in three chapters: Studying a card, Smart Skip, Speech or music
detail: Replaces the separate quick tutorial and full card tour. The ? button and Help open it directly; chapter names along the top jump to any chapter.

Studying a card (9 steps): the full card tour with the essentials folded in — recall and flip, how common the word is, kind of word, dictionary form, meanings, choosing a meaning, how common each meaning is, examples and where they come from, swipe to grade.

Cut: Useful extras and Hear it. Merged: the back's repeated 'The word', 'How often it is said' into 'How common the word is', and 'Where the example is from' into the example note. No more tap-to-continue tasks.
Smart Skip and Speech or music are now pages of their own, showing a copy of the real switch and the Vocabulary picker, with examples in the language being taught.
Each chapter ends with Start studying or Next: <chapter> →.

entries.summary: Skipped cards fill each set bar from the right in light grey
detail: Choose a set: with Smart Skip on, the cards it sets aside take a light-grey share of each set pill from the right, so a level starts partly filled.
The Skipped legend swatch is the same grey; known/practice/new shares are now measured against the full slot.

entries.summary: Smart Skip row on the level box shows more example words, in English
detail: The 'Skipping …' / 'Look-alikes like …' line now lists up to eight words (the row trims to fit), as English words (family, minute, important) instead of the Spanish forms.

entries.summary: Set pills show their word ranks on desktop
detail: Choose a set: on screens 760px and wider each pill reads its frequency-rank range (e.g. 26–50) instead of the set number; phones keep the number.
